new_entities.name: Extensively hydrolyzed infant formula
aliases: extensively hydrolyzed casein or whey formula
new_entities.description: Extensively hydrolyzed infant formula used during early infancy when breastfeeding is insufficient.

new_entities.name: Atopic disease
new_entities.description: Allergic manifestations including atopic dermatitis, food allergy, asthma, wheeze, and rhinitis.

edges.effect_quant: Among high-risk infants compared with standard cow's-milk formula, extensively hydrolyzed formulas show a modest but fairly durable reduction in atopic disease, driven mainly by eczema prevention rather than broad protection against every allergic endpoint.
edges.population: infants, especially those with family history of atopy, receiving extensively hydrolyzed formula instead of standard cow's-milk formula when breastfeeding is insufficient
edges.mechanism: Extensive hydrolysis reduces exposure to intact cow's-milk proteins during a period when immune sensitization can be established. The evidence pattern, strongest for eczema and cow's-milk allergy rather than later asthma or rhinitis, fits a partial early antigen-avoidance effect rather than a complete allergy-prevention strategy.
edges.summary: The best read is modest, endpoint-specific benefit rather than a universal allergy shield. The newer meta-analysis supports reduced eczema and some cow's-milk-allergy benefit compared with standard formula, and the long-running GINI cohort shows that extensively hydrolyzed casein formula produced a durable reduction in allergic manifestations, especially atopic dermatitis, in high-risk children.
edges.caveats: Most of the strongest evidence comes from high-risk infants and from comparison with standard cow's-milk formula, not with breastfeeding. Benefits also differ by hydrolysate type, with casein-based and whey-based products not performing identically.

evidence.notes: Infant Formulas With Partially or Extensively Hydrolyzed Milk Proteins for the Prevention of Allergic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.

effect_quant.comparator: eczema in children older than 2 years fed extensively hydrolyzed formula versus cow's-milk formula

evidence.citation: vonBergA et al 2008 J Allergy Clin Immunol
evidence.notes: Preventive effect of hydrolyzed infant formulas persists until age 6 years: long-term results from the German Infant Nutritional Intervention Study (GINI).

effect_quant.comparator: physician-diagnosed allergic manifestation with extensively hydrolyzed casein formula versus cow's-milk formula

evidence.citation: vonBergA et al 2013 J Allergy Clin Immunol
evidence.notes: Allergies in high-risk schoolchildren after early intervention with cow's milk protein hydrolysates: 10-year results from the German Infant Nutritional Intervention (GINI) study.

effect_quant.comparator: cumulative incidence of any allergic disease with extensively hydrolyzed casein formula versus standard cow's-milk formula
